lines.text: I put it on. And two hundred of me woke *up.*
lines.style: Young man, shouting over a wall of screens switching on, fast and raw, stunned.

lines.text: The doors shut behind me. I didn't *care.*
lines.style: Young man, flat and quick, talking straight to the viewer.
Young man, hushed horror, slow, each short sentence a beat.

lines.text: Good morning, Operator. Shift twelve hundred and *one.*
lines.style: Calm, polite, unsettling announcer voice over an old intercom, warm and welcoming, slow.

lines.text: The tallies weren't days. They were *tries.*
lines.style: Young man, quiet, the floor dropping out from under him, slow.

lines.text: Say the line, Theo. Find Floor *Zero,* and you may leave.
lines.style: Calm, polite, unsettling announcer voice over an old intercom, patient like a teacher, slow.

lines.text: It was never a voice. It was a *script.*
lines.style: Young man, whisper, slow and sick, understanding.

lines.text: Center screen. Floor twelve. A new me. The *key.*
lines.style: Young man, fast staccato whisper, each fragment landing, rising dread.

lines.text: The mic light went *red.* He could hear me.
lines.style: Young man, breath caught, quiet and shaking.

lines.text: Say the line... or tell him the *truth?*
lines.style: Young man, panicking, fast and desperate, torn between two choices.

lines.text: Comment *A* or *B.* You decide what I say.
lines.style: Young man, urgent and direct, speaking straight to the viewer, pleading but steady.

music.title: Floor 0 - The Headset
music.style: Horror thriller score. Starts instantly on a huge electric surge as hundreds of screens switch on, a wall of rising electronic tones, then a slow cold synth pulse like a heartbeat under an intercom, a music box melody twisted and detuned, a single sustained high violin note of dread, then racing ticking and heartbeat to a sudden cut. Instrumental only, no vocals, mixed to sit under a voiceover.
